To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
an ARIMAX time series model with exogenous predictor variables can be used to forecast aquifer discharge in a manner that is useful for water management.
an ARIMAX time‐series model was used to forecast natural aquifer recharge in southern Idaho 4 months in advance, and the model was assessed to be accurate and reliable.
an ARIMAX time‐series model can be used to forecast ESPA aquifer discharge 4 months in advance, given the previous years' discharge and the values of the predictor variable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a statistical model to forecast natural aquifer recharge and discharge in a large, unconfined aquifer.
the development of an ARIMAX model for the ESPA that forecasts aquifer recharge 4 months prior to peak demand.

the development and evaluation of a statistical forecasting tool to predict natural aquifer discharge in the ESPA 4 months ahead of the peak of water demand in the region, which occurs annually during the month of July.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study has demonstrated the feasibility of forecasting natural aquifer discharge using a data‐driven, statistical approach.

the ARIMAX model is a useful tool for forecasting natural aquifer discharge, but that further research is needed to determine the optimal model for forecasting discharge in the ESPA and to determine the optimal predictor variables.

the ARIMAX model forecasts ESPA discharge 4 months before peak water demand with reasonable accuracy, and that this forecast is based on variables that represent the major components of the ESPAs water budget.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a statistical model that uses the most important components of the ESPAs water budget can forecast aquifer discharge 4 months in advance with an efficiency of 0.57, which is a useful level of accuracy.
the ESPA aquifer discharge can be reliably forecast using a statistical time‐series model.

a data‐driven, statistically‐based forecast of aquifer discharge can provide water managers with valuable information for making water‐right mitigation decisions months ahead of the peak demand period.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to forecast the natural aquifer discharge in the ESPA using a statistical approach, which could be useful to water practitioners and managers in the region.
the ESPA is a large, well‐managed aquifer system that can be forecasted using a relatively simple model that is based on readily available, long‐term data.
it is possible to forecast natural aquifer outflow with reasonable accuracy.
